title: GE Aerospace and WZL-2 Sign F404 MRO Support Memorandum of Understanding
summary: KIELCE, POLAND – September 10, 2026 – GE Aerospace (NYSE:GE) and the Military Aviation Works (Wojskowe Zakłady Lotnicze NR 2 S.A. or WZL-2) signed a Memorandum of Understanding
body_markdown:
**KIELCE, POLAND – September 10, 2026** – GE Aerospace (NYSE:GE) and the Military Aviation Works (Wojskowe Zakłady Lotnicze NR 2 S.A. or WZL-2) signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) to explore opportunities to develop maintenance, repair, and overhaul (MRO) services capabilities and depot level maintenance for the F404-GE-102 engine that powers the Polish Air Force’s KAI FA-50 Golden Eagle fighter jets. The MoU was announced by Jakub Gazda, Chief Executive Officer, WZL-2, Zbigniew Matuszczak, Member of the Management Board and Technical Director, WZL-2, and Scott Keating, GE Aerospace’s Defense & Systems Executive Regional General Manager for Europe, at the34th International Defence Industry Exhibition (MSPO) in Kielce, Poland.


“Establishing engine support within Poland is critically important to ensure readiness and availability for our military customer,” said Scott Keating, GE Aerospace’s Defense & Systems Executive Regional General Manager for Europe. “We look forward to working with WZL-2, a well-respected engine MRO provider in Poland, to determine how we can best serve Poland’s needs on the F404 engines to offer this capability in country.”


“Our partnership with GE Aerospace offers us the opportunity to develop our expertise in servicing F404-GE-102 engines. We want to ensure that increasingly advanced maintenance capabilities for equipment used by the Polish Armed Forces are developed and maintained domestically,” said Jakub Gazda, CEO of WZL-2, adding: “This is yet another example of WZL-2’s consistent development of capabilities that strengthen the security and operational independence of the Polish Armed Forces.”


Under the MoU, GE Aerospace and WZL-2 will assess requirements necessary for F404-GE-102 engine maintenance.


The Polish Air Force ordered 48 KAI FA-50 light combat aircraft in 2022. The first 12 were delivered in the FA-50GF ("Gap Filler") configuration in 2023, while the remaining 36 are to be delivered in the FA-50PL configuration. This MoU will cover all 48 F404-GE-102 engines on order as well as spare engines.


The F404 engine is one of the most versatile in its class, continuing to set the standard for performance, simplicity, and capability. More than 4,000 F404 engines have been delivered and have accumulated more than 13 million engine flight hours, including 300 engines that power the T-50, TA-50, and FA-50 Golden Eagle produced in the Republic of Korea.


GE Aerospace’s presence in Poland spans over 30 years with more than 2,300 highly skilled employees based across five locations. Developing the next-generation aerospace technologies for defense and commercial customers, GE Aerospace is proud to remain Poland’s long-term strategic partner.


**About WZL-2**


Wojskowe Zakłady Lotnicze Nr 2 S.A. (WZL-2) is one of Poland's largest aviation companies and is recognized as a strategically important enterprise for the Polish economy and national defense. WZL-2 is part of the Polska Grupa Zbrojeniowa (PGZ) group. WZL-2 offers comprehensive maintenance and modernization services covering both airframes and engines. In addition to its military aviation work, WZL-2 continues to expand its capabilities in civil aviation and unmanned aircraft systems.


**About GE Aerospace**


GE Aerospace is a global aerospace propulsion, services, and systems leader with an installed base of approximately 50,000 commercial and 30,000 military aircraft engines. With a global team of approximately 57,000 employees building on more than a century of innovation and learning, GE Aerospace is committed to inventing the future of flight, lifting people up, and bringing them home safely. Learn more about how GE Aerospace and its partners are defining flight for today, tomorrow, and the future at www.geaerospace.com.
